{{Short description|American statistician and sociologist}}
__NOTOC__
'''Frederick Franklin Stephan''' (May 17, 1903 – August 3, 1971){{r|tas}} was an American [[statistician]] and [[sociologist]], mainly known for his contributions to survey sampling procedures.

==Education and career==
Born in [[Chicago]], he received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] from the [[University of Illinois Chicago|University of Illinois]] in 1924 and an [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] in sociology from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1926.{{r|nyt}} He taught at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] and at [[Cornell University]], before he moved to [[Princeton University]] in 1947, where he was Professor of [[Social statistics|Social Statistics]] until his retirement in 1971, shortly before his death.{{r|poq}}

Together with [[W. Edwards Deming]], he introduced the [[iterative proportional fitting]] algorithm to estimate cell probabilities in contingency tables subject to constraints on the margins.{{r|ipf}}

He served as president of [[American Association for Public Opinion Research|AAPOR]] in 1957–8,{{r|poq}} and as president of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1966.{{r|asapres}}

==Recognition==
He was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1939.

==Personal life==
[[John Stephan]] was his brother.
